surfaces.notes: Only the literal sass-embedded@1.100.0 request acquires sass@1.100.0; the native watcher is omitted and no runtime-asset binding is created.
The synthesized facade exposes the measured sass-embedded namespace through require() and import().

The finite oracle pins repeated path/string compilation, sync/async disposal outcomes, exact post-dispose errors, lifecycle export accessors, exported constructor/prototype descriptors, and exact public method name, arity, placement, and identity within and across instances.

renderSync output, stats keys, and legacy-js-api deprecation match the exact Node oracle.

divergence.surface: Sync compile with an async importer
divergence.notes: Pure Sass throws a clean Exception; real sass-embedded deadlocks the event loop. Rifty preserves the loud throw and records the deliberate divergence.

unsupported.notes: Exact embedded starts a refed Dart child before rejecting construction; the no-runtime-asset facade cannot reproduce that lifecycle.

Exact embedded exposes live Dart process and dispatcher internals. The no-runtime facade does not fabricate those values; ownKeys and each get/has/own-descriptor access to the observed embedded-only names stay loud, while pure-only _disposed remains absent.

Every request except the literal 1.100.0 is rejected before registry or VFS work. Lockfile replay reifies the attested 1.100.0 pin without re-litigating npm-recorded ranges (npm ci parity, ADR-0361); any other pinned version still throws.
The materialized sass bin is a loud gap; the acquired pure-Sass bin never leaks.
Watch mode is outside the proven facade; @parcel/watcher is never acquired.
No TypeScript declarations or types target are published; exact declaration materialization remains unsupported.

limitations: Only the exact sass-embedded@1.100.0 facade over exact sass@1.100.0 and the finite differential rows are claimed by this contract.
Supported rows are proven by the exact Node differential and real Chromium Vite acceptance; named unsupported surfaces remain explicit failures.
The sync-compile async-importer deadlock is an explicit deliberate divergence, never a parity claim.
